chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar from Ibn Abi Ya'fur said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the use of kohl (eye makeup) for the fasting person, so he said: 'There is no harm with it, for it is not food that is eaten.'
ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ibn Abi Yafur asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the permissibility of applying kohl while fasting, to which the Imam replies that there is no harm in it. The Imam’s reasoning hinges on the distinction between substances that are consumed as food and those applied externally, establishing a precedent for medical treatments that do not involve ingestion. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between nullifiers of the fast and permissible external remedies.
